## Summary

Google's Docs API now supports programmatic comments via `documents.batchUpdate` (`insertComment`, Workspace Developer Preview) — the first real path to **anchored** comments since the `kix.*` limitation. This PR wires it into `comment --quote`:

- `--quote "doc text"` locates the first occurrence of the quote in the document body (retrying with smart-quote/dash folding, same as `edit --normalize`) and anchors an `insertComment` request to that range → a real anchored comment, highlighted in the Docs UI.
- **Transparent fallback** when the preview isn't available: project not enrolled (400 for the unknown request field — including the live-observed `"Invalid requests[0]: No request set."` shape, where the server silently drops the unrecognized field), comment-only access (403, can't `batchUpdate`), or quote text not found. Falls back to the existing Drive `quotedFileContent` path, so behavior for non-preview users is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Terse output gains an `(anchored)` suffix on success; `--json`/`--plain` report `anchored` true/false whenever `--quote` is given.
- New `insert_comment` helper in `gdoc/api/docs.py`; `PreviewUnavailableError` sentinel (a `GdocError` subclass) in `gdoc/util.py` — internal only, never surfaces as a failure.
- Release 0.14.0: version bumped in `pyproject.toml` + `gdoc/__init__.py`, CHANGELOG entry, README section under Comments.

## Test plan

- 19 new tests in `tests/test_anchored_comment.py`: request/response shapes, every preview-gate error variant (unknown-name 400, no-request-set 400, 403), `commentUpdateState` partial-failure handling, 401/404 passthrough, CLI anchored/fallback/no-quote flows, JSON output, state-patch tracking. Full suite: **1232 passed**.
- Live smoke test against a real (non-enrolled) project: created a scratch doc, `comment --quote` returned `"anchored": false` via the fallback, `cat --comments` displayed the comment inline at the right line, doc deleted. This is what caught the undocumented "No request set." error shape.
- The enrolled (anchored) path can't be live-tested until a project has preview access; it's covered by unit tests against Google's documented request/response schemas.

title: feat: real anchored comments via Docs API insertComment (developer preview)
